gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Bluetooth stops working underwater (Shokz: "No, Bluetooth connectivity is not functional underwater with OpenSwim Pro"), so for swimming the music has to be stored on the headphones themselves, as on the MOJAWA Purra Swim and Run Plus with 32 GB each.
standout_why: ChatGPT ran no searches and got no result pages, so there was no rival page to compare against. Its answer was the only rival. It says bone conduction has 'weaker bass' and 'does not bypass' hearing risk, but it never mentions water, swimming, Bluetooth range or onboard storage. Its table only covers running and cycling. The bass point is partly covered already. The underwater Bluetooth limit is entirely new. I scored it 2 rather than 3 because it decides the pick only for shoppers who swim, not for the general question.
decides: For swimmers it decides the pick. A Bluetooth-only bone conduction model such as the Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 (IP55, no storage) cannot play music during laps, and regular headphones are out entirely. They need an IP68 model with built-in MP3 storage: the MOJAWA Purra Swim ($169.99) or the cheaper Run Plus ($99.99). For runners and cyclists it changes nothing. The OpenRun Pro 2 stays the pick there, and Shokz moves low frequencies to an air-conduction driver because strong vibration is a main complaint about bone conduction. That supports ChatGPT's point about weaker bass and explains why the best-sounding bone conduction model isn't purely bone conduction.

findings.label: Bluetooth underwater
findings.value: Does not work; underwater listening must use the onboard MP3 mode
findings.source_title: Shokz OpenSwim Pro Support - Setup, Usage & Troubleshooting Guide
findings.note: Verbatim FAQ answer: "No, Bluetooth connectivity is not functional underwater with OpenSwim Pro." Read on Shokz's Canadian support page because shokz.com (US) returned HTTP 429 on every try. The page explains this as water interfering with the wireless signal (paraphrased by the fetch tool, not verbatim). The limit comes from 2.4 GHz radio physics, not from Shokz's design, so it applies to every Bluetooth headphone.

The listing says 'completely phone-free with 32GB built-in storage'. The listing does not itself say that Bluetooth fails underwater (see unsourced). A WebFetch of the HTML page was rate-limited (429).

findings.label: Why the best-sounding bone conduction model adds an air driver
findings.value: Low frequencies go to an air-conduction driver; bone conduction handles the rest
findings.source_title: The Sound Quality of Shokz OpenRun Pro 2
findings.note: Verbatim: "Strong vibrations are one of the main criticisms of bone conduction headphones." Bass frequencies "are handled by the air conduction driver to deliver a deeper, more booming bass," "assigning the low frequencies to the air conduction driver. This creates minimal vibrations for less tactile feedback." The page gives no crossover frequency.

unsourced: A statement on MOJAWA's own pages (product page or manual) that Bluetooth fails underwater. A search snippet credited this to the Purra Swim manual on manuals.plus, which returned 403. The product page HTML returned 429.
